378YE Winter Solstice Announcements by t.d: The Minister for Historical Research approved four separate research commissions, carried out through the civil service: the runeforge at Gildenheim in Skarsind, the ancient Urizen spire known as the Claw of the Heavens, Emperor Barabbas' plans to invade the Grendel, and the origins of the Hallowing ceremony. Though announced together, each counted as a separate announcement for the purposes of a Synod veto. Progress was unknown at the time of recording; the expected outcome was that research reports would be compiled and presented to the Minister.

n.Grendel: Research was commissioned into Emperor Barabbas' plans to invade the Grendel, promising the Empire fresh insight into its historical designs on that foreign nation.
n.Urizen: The ancient Urizen spire called the Claw of the Heavens was made a subject of commissioned historical research.
n.Wintermark: The runeforge at Gildenheim, in the Wintermark territory of Skarsind, was among the four subjects of commissioned historical research.

t.Skarsind: Historical research was commissioned into the runeforge at Gildenheim in Skarsind, with a report to be presented to the Minister.

378YE Winter Solstice winds of fortune.d: Vermin from the realm of Night were sighted in Morrow and threatened its mana and herb production. Segura's full restoration prompted celebrations that the Synod, Senate and Bourse might capitalise on. A coordinated cult of Anarchists sabotaged military units in Miekarova. Soldiers of the two orc legions developed a friendly rivalry the Synod might exploit. In Miaren a Winter enchantment of magnitude 50 brought Navarr extra bounty, but also nightmares, deaths among the weak and troubles for the draughir. In Wintermark, The Strength of Tradition set Suaq, Kallavesi and Steinr against one another and strained its armies, possibly through Thule sorcery. Kallavesa's mana crystals grew sluggish and brittle.

n.Navarr: Navarr in Miaren enjoyed unexpected prosperity in their herb gardens, mines, forests, farms, businesses and mana sites, along with extra Synod votes from congregations. This came at the cost of nightmares among children, sleepless elders and draughir struggling to control their territorial instincts.
n.The Brass Coast: Celebrations swept the Brass Coast's Segura after its full restoration to the Empire, offering the Synod, Senate and Bourse a chance to capitalise on the popular mood.
n.Thule: Thule dark magic was named as the most likely cause of the influence dividing Wintermark, since the Thule have a vested interest in destabilising the nation's armies to speed their conquest.
n.Urizen: Boggarts from the realm of Night infested Urizen's territory of Morrow, threatening its mana and herb production and possibly that of surrounding territories.
n.Varushka: A coordinated cult of Anarchists carried out sabotage across Varushka's Miekarova, aimed chiefly at military units in order to disrupt the Imperial war effort.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark fell under The Strength of Tradition, which split Suaq, Kallavesi and Steinr into quarrelling factions and strained the Fist of the Mountain and Green Shield. Halls dominated by a single tradition prospered, while three distinct egregores fed fearful speculation.

t.Kallavesa: Mana sites across the Kallavesa marshes grew sluggish, and their crystals formed slowly, looked dull or crumbled to dust. Mystics feared a separate threat, but spreading parochialism kept anyone beyond the Kallavesi from listening, and mana yields could fall significantly if the problem worsened.
t.Miaren: A Winter enchantment of magnitude 50 lay over Miaren for the three months after the Autumn Equinox, giving every Navarr resource there an extra rank. It also brought a cruel edge of dying weak plants and animals, nightmares and troubled draughir before it faded towards the Solstice.
t.Miekarova: Anarchist sabotage and disruption spread across Miekarova, targeting military units in a coordinated attempt to undermine the Imperial war effort.
t.Morrow: Boggarts from the realm of Night were sighted in Morrow and could harm its mana and herb production and that of neighbouring territories.
t.Segura: Segura celebrated its full restoration to the Empire, creating an opportunity for the Synod, Senate and Bourse to harness the public sentiment.

378YE Winter Solstice winds of war.d: In Karsk, Imperial forces aided by citadels, the Summer legion of Jaheris, Varushkan undead, Spring healing waters and the Golden Axe's strategic insight drove the Thule out of Nitrost and reclaimed the territory. In Sermersuaq, the Thule, allied with Summer knights, fought the Empire to near deadlock but took the upper foothills, controlling a little over half the Silver Peaks while failing to reach the Ice Caves; about a thousand Imperial soldiers died. The Granite Pillar and Quiet Step entered Reikos, found it ravaged under a fearful miasma, and barely took Tabernacle. Over 25,000 Imperial troops broke out of Holberg, took Holmauer and half of Rebeshof, and prepared to besiege the Druj castle as Druj reinforcements arrived.

n.Dawn: Dawnish armies fought on several fronts: the Eastern Sky cleared die-hard Lasambrian raiders from Segura, the Hounds of Glory were singled out by Summer knights in the Silver Peaks, and the Golden Sun camped before the walls of Rebeshof.
n.Druj: The Druj lost Holmauer and were driven back behind the walls of their castle in Rebeshof, though fresh banners of the snake, scorpion and crimson lizard arrived. In Reikos they held firm, harrying the Imperial advance under a dreadful miasma and a white toad clan banner.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: in an interlude at Spiral, a Highborn magister complains there is no fight in the Grendel, while his companion insists they will come in time.
n.Highguard: The Granite Pillar returned to Reikos to find its people slain or enslaved, its chapters' banners defiled and Highborn toiling at the Vigilant Swan, and won only a narrow foothold. Highborn soldiers also joined the successful breakout from Holberg.
n.Navarr: The Quiet Step fought beside the Granite Pillar in Reikos, and Navarr scouts spread across the ruined territory in small groups to report back to their general.
n.The Brass Coast: The Lasambrian orcs largely left Segura as agreed, and the Red Wind Corsairs and Fire of the South fought hard in the Silver Peaks, where Summer knights sought out the Freeborn.
n.The League: League soldiers were among the 25,000 Imperial troops who broke out of Holberg, and engineers who once marched under the Towerjacks' banner helped bring down Holmauer's last keep.
n.Thule: The Thule were driven out of Karsk despite their warlocks, but in Sermersuaq, aided by Summer knights and Otkodov-bred ogres, they took the upper foothills and now control a little over half the Silver Peaks.
n.Urizen: The Urizen Citadel Guard fought in Karsk alongside the Summer legion of Jaheris, and Urizen hosts kept a Highborn magister and his companions standing watch in a castle in Spiral.
n.Varushka: Karsk returned to Imperial hands thanks to the Golden Axe's strategic brilliance, the Black Thorns' walking dead and a draughir general commanding a ghostly legion, though it was unclear whether the Senate would uphold the Varushkan claim.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark suffered tremendous loss of life as the Winter Sun and its allies fought the Thule to a near standstill in Sermersuaq, keeping them from the Ice Caves but ceding the upper foothills.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: the Strong Reeds were force-marched from distant Astolat to reinforce the armies in Holberg.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: a brief interlude shows Captain Drummer unexpectedly facing three ships somewhere in the bay.
t.Holberg: Imperial armies poured out of the city, took Holmauer, secured half of Rebeshof and prepared to besiege the Druj castle, though Druj reinforcements meant the war for Holberg was not over.
t.Karsk: Karsk became Imperial territory again after a season of magical wonders and bloody fighting, with the Thule pushed back to makeshift defences in the east and north.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: ogres bred in the pits of Otkodov served as living battering rams, and the Empire sought to drive the Thule back towards it.
t.Reikos: Imperial forces found Reikos devastated, its people slain or enslaved, a Druj citadel standing where High Chalcis's gardens had been and a miasma of dread over everything. They gained only a small foothold.
t.Segura: All three Lasambrian forces withdrew as agreed, leaving a few hundred die-hards and some bandits from Anduz to the Scorrero for the Dawnish to root out over several months.
t.Sermersuaq: Thule banners nearly doubled in Sermersuaq, and Spring magic filled its waters with life, healing non-fatal wounds even as about a thousand Imperial soldiers died in the fighting.
t.Spiral: An interlude shows a restless Highborn magister standing watch in a Urizen castle in Spiral, troubled by dreams of something to the north-east and told the Grendel will come in time.
t.Tsirku: Mentioned in passing: the great aurora dancing above Tsirku lit the cold nights over Sermersuaq.

r.Holberg/Holmauer: Holmauer fell to the Empire after fierce fighting across its broken walls, its last keep brought down by the Wolves of War's boulders. Its suburbs are now ruins.
r.Holberg/Rebeshof: The Empire consolidated its hold on half of Rebeshof, driving the Scorpion banner behind the castle walls, and its armies prepared to lay siege.
r.Karsk/Nitrost: The Thule were pushed back out of the hills of Nitrost at the end of the season.
r.Reikos/Riverwatch: The Granite Pillar and Quiet Step more or less drove the Druj from the trapped ruins of Tabernacle, but much remained to be done before Riverwatch was liberated.
r.Sermersuaq/East Floes: Mentioned in passing: East Floes was among the places whose waters teemed with fish and life under Spring magic.
r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: The Thule took the upper foothills and now hold a little over half the Silver Peaks, stripping its resources, but were kept from the Ice Caves and their star metal.

Accept Grendel proposal.d: An ambassador from the Grendel Salt Lord of Dubhtraig brought an agreement before the Imperial Senate. Proposed by Kahraman and seconded by Feroz, the motion accepted it: one Grendel army would leave Spiral in return for the Empire refraining from raiding Dubhtraig for one year, with further negotiations possible afterwards with this Salt Lord or others. The motion changed no law and was a statement of principle by the Senate. The Grendel remained barbarians, and raiding their fleets remained entirely legal.

n.Grendel: The Salt Lord of Dubhtraig secured the Senate's acceptance of a deal under which Dubhtraig would be spared Imperial raids for a year in return for withdrawing one Grendel army from Spiral, though Grendel fleets remained lawful targets for raiders.

t.Spiral: Under the accepted agreement, the Grendel occupiers of Spiral were to remove one of their armies from the territory in exchange for a year without Imperial raids on Dubhtraig.

Address boggart infestation in Morrow.d: The motion set out to trap the boggarts plaguing Morrow, which had been causing the loss of mana from the territory's mana sites. It passed at a cost of 25 thrones, and the Synod passed a statement of principle saying it had no intention of vetoing it. The 25 thrones were disbursed to Senator Sarvos. Together with a successful quest by the Academy, the traps prevented further loss of mana from Morrow's mana sites. In an unexpected side benefit, boggart faeces was harvested and used to enhance the herb gardens of Morrow. The wider campaign outcome is recorded as unknown.

n.Urizen: Urizen's senator Sarvos proposed the motion and received the 25 thrones, and with the Academy's successful quest the nation stopped boggarts draining mana from its sites in Morrow.

t.Morrow: Boggarts infesting Morrow were trapped, ending the loss of mana from the territory's mana sites, and their droppings were put to use enriching Morrow's herb gardens.

Anarchy in Miekarova.d: The civil service reported a coordinated campaign of anarchy auras and sabotage in Miekarova aimed at the infrastructure that supports smaller military units, leaving soldiers demoralised and cut off from letters and supplies. No cult claimed responsibility, though the incidents followed the Senate building's consecration to anarchy and at least one Synod-condemned individual remained at large. Left unchecked, the units would suffer a massive loss of effectiveness while businesses enjoyed a moderate, unsustainable rise in demand. The options set out were militia funding, a military sweep relocating anarchists to a neighbouring territory, exorcism, auras of Vigilance, or disrupting the cult's leadership. The Assembly of Vigilance chose the auras, naming Vitomir Vardov to coordinate them, which limits the disruption while leaving the business boost intact.

n.Varushka: Varushkan military units operating out of Miekarova faced sabotage and demoralisation. The Varushkan National Assembly was one body that could have named someone to lead exorcisms, but the response came instead from the Vigilance Assembly through Vitomir Vardov.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark's territory of Skarsind was listed as a possible destination if the Senate had ordered anarchists swept out of Miekarova and relocated.

t.Karov: Mentioned in passing: Karov was named as a neighbouring territory to which anarchists could have been forcibly relocated under a Senate-approved military sweep.
t.Miekarova: Anarchy auras and sabotage across Miekarova threatened a massive loss of effectiveness for military units based there, while impulse spending gave local businesses a temporary boost. Vitomir Vardov was named to raise auras of Vigilance throughout the territory in response.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind was named as a neighbouring territory to which anarchists could have been forcibly relocated under a Senate-approved military sweep.
t.Volodmartz: Mentioned in passing: Volodmartz was named as a neighbouring territory to which anarchists could have been forcibly relocated under a Senate-approved military sweep.

Archive:378YE Winter Solstice Imperial t.d: The page lists the senators for every Imperial territory, alongside Senate offices such as the Conscience of the Senate, Lisabetta Giacomi von Holberg, the Admiral, Sendero i Hazana i Guerra, and Syn Nighthaven as Wisest Senator. It names the generals of each nation's armies, the Synod's cardinals, gatekeepers and other religious offices, the six Archmagi and the order grandmasters, and the holders of Imperial and national Bourse seats with their winning bids. The Cardinal of Vigilance and the Auditor of Senatorial Accountability were vacant after their holders died. The Great Forest at Reikos and the Great Pits of Ennerlund were held by the Druj and withheld from auction.

n.Dawn: Dawn's senators were Hector de Rondell, Escalados deCarsenere and Valentin Ivarovich Orzel, and its generals led the Hounds of Glory, the Golden Sun and the Eastern Sky. Agnetha De Rondell served as Cardinal of Wisdom, while the Vigilance cardinalcy was vacant following the demise of Marrok de Carsenere.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are noted as holding the Great Forest at Reikos and the Great Pits of Ennerlund, which would not be auctioned until those territories became Imperial again.
n.Highguard: Highguard held the seats of Bastion, Casinea and Necropolis, and its generals led the Seventh Wave, the Granite Pillar and the Valiant Pegasus. Its citizens also held the Cardinal seats of Courage and Loyalty and the Gatekeeper posts of Pride and Vigilance.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs' generals were Morgur Bloodcrow of the Winter Sun and Braka of the Summer Storm. Irontide Bruc was Advisor on Orc Affairs, Irontide Rad was Quartermaster General and Irontide Vio held the Steel Fist.
n.Navarr: Navarr's senators were Rhain, Syn Nighthaven, who had also been chosen as Wisest Senator, and Caerwyn Summer Crow. Its generals were Carr Foxden of the Black Thorns and Merryn Farkas of the Quiet Step.
n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast held four Senate seats, and its generals led the Red Wind Corsairs and the Fire of the South. Sendero i Hazana i Guerra served as Admiral, and Edmundo i Jannat i Riqueza as Grandmaster of the Golden Pyramid.
n.The League: The League's senators were Mirislav, Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato and Gant Archama, and Gabriel Barossa led the Wolves of War. Leaguers also held many Bourse seats and the Conscience of the Senate, while the Auditor of Senatorial Accountability was vacant after the demise of Tolya Orbardenko.
n.The Marches: The Marches were represented by Orrick, Bridget Eastville and Henry Ward, and its generals led the Drakes, the Strong Reeds and the Bounders. Peter Keeper of Kingstoke was Cardinal of Prosperity, and Silent John was Gatekeeper of Ambition.
n.Urizen: Urizen's senators were Ariadne, Marissa Shatterspire and Cato, and Tanwyn Ankarien commanded the Citadel Guard. Solas of Urizen held the post of High Exorcist.
n.Varushka: Varushka held four Senate seats, and its generals led the Northern Eagle and the Golden Axe. Varushkans also served as Cardinal of Pride and Imperial Inquisitor, and held the Grandmastership of the Shuttered Lantern.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's senators were Hengest Dun, Uskolli, Atte and Jorma Steelhail, and its generals led the Green Shield Army and the Fist of the Mountain. Beodun Snowlock was Bishop of the Way, and Wintermark citizens held the Stonefield Ice Caves and the Brilliant Shore.

t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: listed as the seat of Senator Jada of Ravensfell.

t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: listed as the seat of Senator Cato.

r.Holberg/Ennerlund: The Great Pits of Ennerlund were held by the Druj and withheld from the Bourse auction until Holberg was once again an Imperial territory.

Assignment of Karsk II.d: Karsk had been retaken by Imperial forces during the Autumn of 378YE, and this motion before the Senate sought to assign the territory to one of the Imperial nations. It was proposed by Mitwold and seconded by Karov. As a result, Karsk became part of the nation of Varushka. The territory was noted to remain insecure, however, as the Thule still controlled three of its seven regions, leaving the reconquest incomplete.

n.Thule: The Thule lost Karsk to the Empire but still held three of its seven regions, keeping the territory insecure.
n.Varushka: Varushka gained Karsk as part of its nation following the Imperial reconquest, though the territory was not yet fully secure.

t.Karsk: Karsk was formally allocated to Varushka after its reconquest, but the Thule still controlled three of its seven regions.

Boggarts in Morrow.d: A Spire's mana site in Morrow was found raided by boggarts, which camouflage themselves and feed on pooled magic. Left alone, they would massively cut Morrow's mana site output, though their potent but short-lived faeces would moderately boost herb gardens and farms. The civil service set out historical responses: Academy boggart hunts, relocating the swarm by lures to an adjacent territory as in Empress Mariika's reign, Nicovar's boggart traps protecting mana while harvesting the manure, or seeking Sadogua's uncertain intervention. The Senate chose to trap the boggarts and reduce the impact on mana sites, the response that preserves both the mana supply and the boost to herb gardens.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: the boggarts are likened to naga yeomen far from Dawn, and Dawn's Astolat is cited as a past infestation.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Navarr's Miaren is cited as the territory that once received boggarts relocated from Astolat.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: a First Interregnum tale tells of Sadogua moving boggarts from Kahraman to Madruga, both now Brass Coast territories.
n.Urizen: Urizen's mana sites in Morrow faced a massive loss of production to boggarts, which the Senate's trapping response was chosen to reduce while its herb gardens and farms stood to benefit from the boggarts' manure.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: boggarts were once lured from Astolat to Miaren under a scheme from Empress Mariika's reign.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: in a possibly apocryphal First Interregnum story, Sadogua removed boggarts from Kahraman at an Archmage of Night's request.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: the same story claims Sadogua relocated Kahraman's boggarts to Madruga with their numbers swollen.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: Miaren once received boggarts relocated from Astolat, gaining herb production while being mana poor at the time.
t.Morrow: Boggarts infested Morrow's mana sites, threatening a massive fall in mana production; the Senate chose to trap them, protecting the mana supply while the creatures' manure could enrich local herb gardens and farms.

r.Kahraman/Gambit: Mentioned in passing: the region is not named on the page, which refers only to Kahraman as a whole in the tale of Sadogua's removal of boggarts.

Construct Faraden embassy.d: Proposed by Therunin and seconded by Mitwold, the motion sought Senate funds to build a Faraden embassy in Anduz. It passed at 80 Thrones, and the money was paid to Senator Therunin. The project needed 20 wains of weirwood and 20 wains of white granite, less than the standard cost for an embassy, plus one season's work and an upkeep of 5 Thrones. The Faraden would only recognise the embassy once the Towers of Anduz had been rebuilt. Caerwyn supplied 20 wains of weirwood and 18 of white granite after the Spring Equinox 379YE, and the last 2 wains of granite after the Summer Solstice 379YE. On completion the embassy would create the Imperial title of Ambassador to Faraden.

n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn gain a diplomatic link to the Faraden on their own soil at Anduz, although its recognition depends on the Towers of Anduz being rebuilt first.

t.Segura: The embassy is to be built in Anduz in Segura, which makes the territory the seat of the Empire's future Ambassador to Faraden once the Towers of Anduz are rebuilt.

Construct college of magic in Morrow.d: Proposed by the senator for Redoubt and seconded by the senator for Kallavesa, the motion sought permission, but no funding, to raise a Summer college in Morrow. Corvus, Archmage of Summer, was called as an expert witness. Because it followed designs from the Eternal Meraud, its cost differed from a standard college: 90 wains of White Granite, 30 wains of Mithril, 20 wains of Weirwood and 35 Thrones in labour, with a year to build and upkeep of 25 Thrones. Had it been completed, it would have created the Imperial title of Dean, filled through a Declaration of Candidacy in the Conclave. The commission lapsed.

n.Urizen: The senators for the Urizen territories of Redoubt and Kallavesa proposed and seconded a Summer college in their nation's land of Morrow, but the commission lapsed before it was built.

t.Morrow: Morrow was the intended site of a Summer College of Magic built to the Eternal Meraud's designs, but the commission lapsed and the college was never constructed.

Construct the Glorious Fountain of Dusk.d: Proposed by the senator for Zenith and seconded by the senator for Karsk, the motion would create the sinecure to produce 9 crystal mana each season. It required 10 wains of mithril, 20 crowns in labour and three months to build, with no upkeep. Cato, senator for Zenith, later supplied the mithril and 2 thrones 4 crowns after the Autumn Equinox 379. Once complete, it would create the Imperial title Keeper of the Glorious Fountain. This national lifetime position would be appointed by unanimous decision of the Urizen senators and could be revoked by the Urizen assembly, the General Assembly or the Assembly of Nine.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Dawn appears only in the sinecure's name, the Glorious Fountain of Dusk and Dawn, and plays no part in the motion.
n.Urizen: Urizen would gain a mana-producing sinecure in Morrow, funded by its own senator for Zenith. Its senators would appoint the Keeper of the Glorious Fountain, and the Urizen assembly would be among those able to revoke the title.

t.Morrow: The Glorious Fountain of Dusk and Dawn was to be built in Morrow, where it would produce 9 crystal mana each season.

Define Jarmish embassy.d: The motion assigned the Jarmish embassy a remote principality to work with, specifically requesting that Jarm construct its embassy to the Empire in Rigia, a port city in the eastern Principalities. The decision was expected to lead the Principalities of Jarm to recognise the Imperial embassy in Cargo, formalising diplomatic ties in both directions. Oswi Twice-Burned was appointed Imperial Ambassador to Jarm at the Autumn Equinox 378YE.

n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Urizen is not named in the motion; it is linked only through the Imperial embassy in Cargo, which Jarm was expected to recognise.

t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: the page does not name Redoubt; it is linked through the Imperial embassy in Cargo, which the decision was expected to see Jarm recognise.

Disburse funds to Miekarova militia.d: Proposed by the Senator for Miekarova and seconded by the Senator for Volodmartz, the motion sought funds to deal with anarchy cultists causing disruption in Miekarova. It passed at 26 thrones, which were disbursed to the Senator for Miekarova to pay for the militia. The disruption had been hampering military units based in the territory, reducing their effectiveness when raiding or when assisting Imperial armies. The 26 thrones were enough only to partially mitigate this, lessening but not removing the penalty to those units.

n.Varushka: Varushkan senators led the effort to fund action against the anarchy cultists, and Varushkan military units based in Miekarova saw their hampered effectiveness partially restored.

t.Miekarova: A militia funded with 26 thrones was raised to crush the anarchy cultists in Miekarova, partially easing the disruption to military units based there without ending it.

Fortify Miekarova.d: Proposed by the senator for Volodmartz and seconded by the senator for Zenith, the motion would have authorised a rank one fortification in Miekarova. Its standard costs would have been 80 white granite and 20 Thrones, with a year to construct and an upkeep of 10 Thrones per season. The Senate defeated the motion, so no fortification was commissioned and no construction took place.

n.Varushka: Varushkan senators from Volodmartz sought stronger defences for one of their own territories against the northern barbarians, but the defeat of the motion left Miekarova without the new fortress.

t.Miekarova: Miekarova would have received a new rank one fortification against threats from the Northern Barbarians, but the motion failed and no fortress was raised there.

Friendly rivalry.d: Orc military units deployed away from their parent armies increasingly fought alongside one another. This built stronger links between them but also sparked competition in sparring, athletics and claims over which army had done more for The Plan. The civil service saw no harm in it. Imperial prognosticators judged that a statement of principle from the Imperial Orc National Assembly praising only one army's contribution to the Imperial Orc ambition would give that army's units a temporary but significant boost in morale and effectiveness. Praising both armies would have no appreciable effect. Atla raised a statement praising the Winter Sun alone, and its units duly received the boost.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are not named, though the orc soldiers boast of the barbarian orcs they have killed, and one asks who broke the siege of Holberg.
n.Imperial Orcs: The rivalry between the Summer Storm and Winter Sun drew the two armies closer while sharpening their pride. Atla's statement of principle in the Imperial Orc assembly gave the Winter Sun's units a temporary surge of morale and battlefield effectiveness.

t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: a Summer Storm soldier cites the breaking of the siege of Holberg as evidence of his army's achievements.

Raise Dawnish army.d: The motion proposed raising a fourth Dawnish army, to be based in Astolat. It was proposed by Semmerholm and seconded by Weirwater. The standard costs would have been 250 mithril in materials, one year to construct, and upkeep of 50 Thrones per season once complete. The Senate defeated the motion, so construction of the new army never began and Dawn's military strength remained unchanged.

n.Dawn: Dawn was denied a fourth army when the Senate defeated the motion, despite the backing of Semmerholm and Weirwater.

t.Astolat: Astolat would have been the place where the new Dawnish army was raised, but no army was begun there after the motion failed.

Raise Freeborn navy.d: The Senator for Madruga proposed the motion and Kahraman seconded it. It passed at a cost of 500 thrones, which were paid to Senator Madruga. Construction takes a year and the navy has an upkeep of 50 thrones per season. Thanks to recent victories in Segura and a judgement of the Assembly of Pride, it needed only 200 wains of weirwood instead of the standard costs. Anwar i Del Toro i Riquezza supplied that weirwood in four shipments of 50 wains, after each summit from Winter Solstice 378YE to Autumn Equinox 379YE. The finished navy creates the Imperial title of admiral.

n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn gained a new Imperial navy, built in their own shipyards and largely supplied with weirwood by the Freeborn Anwar i Del Toro i Riquezza.

t.Madruga: The navy was built at the Atalaya shipyards in Madruga, and Madruga's senator proposed the motion and received the 500 thrones to fund it.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: recent victories in Segura are cited as one reason the navy needed only 200 wains of weirwood.

Rebuild the Towers of Anduz.d: Proposed by the senator for Segura and seconded by Miaren in Winter 378YE, the motion sought permission to rebuild the Towers of Anduz to boost trade with the Faraden and the prosperity of the Empire. It passed in principle without requesting funds. The work required 50 wains of white granite and three months to construct, with no upkeep. The granite was provided by Avisena i Ezmara i Guerra after the Spring Equinox 379YE. Once completed, the towers protect merchant caravans travelling through the Lasambrian Hills, and businesses in Segura operated by Freeborn citizens gain a share of additional money from improved trade with the Faraden and the Iron Confederacy.

n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn-run businesses in Segura stand to gain extra money from the improved trade with the Faraden and the Iron Confederacy, and a Freeborn citizen, Avisena i Ezmara i Guerra, supplied the white granite for the work.

t.Segura: The Towers of Anduz were restored in Segura as a great work, guarding merchant caravans crossing the Lasambrian Hills after Segura's own senator proposed the motion.

The Glorious Advance.d: With Segura fully back under Imperial control, celebrations ran strongest in the Brass Coast and Dawn, whose soldiers died to restore it. Prognosticators advised that a Statement of Principle from the Assembly of Pride validating a single nation would channel this mood. Celebrating Dawn, alongside a Senate motion at the Winter Solstice 378YE to found a Dawnish army, would save 50 mithril. Celebrating the Brass Coast, alongside a motion for a Freeborn navy, would save 50 weirwood. Celebrating both nations would dilute the effect and lose the benefit. The General Assembly could supersede the Assembly of Pride's judgement only after Pride had ruled. Pride celebrated the Brass Coast, aiding the mustering of the Freeborn Storm.

n.Dawn: The Eastern Sky and Hounds of Glory, two Dawnish armies, fought in the liberation, and a Pride statement celebrating Dawn could have saved 50 mithril on a new Dawnish army. The Assembly of Pride chose the Brass Coast instead, so Dawn did not receive the benefit.
n.The Brass Coast: The Red Wind Corsairs helped drive the Lasambrians off the Iron Plains, and the Assembly of Pride celebrated Freeborn efforts in reclaiming Segura. The resulting zeal helped muster the Freeborn Storm navy.

t.Segura: Segura was returned fully to Imperial control after the Lasambrians were pushed to the negotiating table and then off Imperial land.

r.Segura/Iron Plains: The Red Wind Corsairs were credited with driving the Lasambrians off the Iron Plains while the Dawnish armies engaged Summer realm soldiers.
